borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development fails to provide a safe and accessible parking arrangement that could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore likely to add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site and would create an unsafe and unlawful parking arrangement, compromising the existing footpath.  As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision:- National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)- Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)- Policy DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)

The proposal fails to provide sufficient information regarding the location of bin storage and waste management and fails to provide sufficient information regarding the location and provision of secure cycle storage that is functional, well-located and secure. The proposal lacks clarity and is therefore unacceptable and contrary to the following:- Policy T5 of the London Plan (March 2021)- Policy DMT3 and Part 3 in policy DMSI 8 of the Local Plan (September 2024)- The Council's Planning Advice Note on Waste and Recycling Provisions in New and Refurbished Residential Developments (dated 20/05/2021).

The proposed flat would fail to comply with the internal space standards for a 1-bed 1-person flat  and would result in the provision of  sub-standard quality of accommodation. The proposed flat would not provide sufficient access to daylight and sunlight and would not be sufficiently ventilated, failing to be dual aspect. The proposal has also failed to clearly outline the provision of private external amenity space. The application is therefore unacceptable and contrary to the following:DCLG Technical Housing Standards (nationally described space standard) (DCLG, March 2015) (as amended)Policy D6,  Policy H1 and H2 and Table 3.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy SP3, DMD 1 and Part 6 of policy DMNE1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)Housing Design Standards LPG (June 2023)

The proposed development, by reason of siting, scale, and design would result in the intensification of thean area typically  reserved for private rear amenity space of the existing dwellings. The proposal would therefore disrupt the established pattern of development within the area, causing harm to the surrounding character and appearance, and would cause harm to the significance of the non-designated heritage asset: Becontree Estate. As such, the proposed development would be contrary to the following policies which seek to ensure that development proposals respect the existing character and appearance and preserve or enhance historic distinctiveness: National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D1, D4, and HC1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2, DMD1, DMD4 and DMD6 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)
description: Retrospective application for the conversion of the single storey rear outbuilding into a studio flat
